stem.text: Let \( r = k(z) \) be a twice-differentiable function. Suppose that \( \left. \frac{dr}{dz} \right|_{z=3} = 6 \). Write this statement in prime notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( k'(3) = 6 \), so the rate of change of r with respect to z when z = 3 is 6.

worked_solution.text: In \( \left. \frac{dr}{dz} \right|_{z=3} \) the function is k, the independent variable is z, and the derivative is evaluated at z = 3, so the statement is about one input only.
In prime notation the same statement is \( k'(3) = 6 \).
It says that the rate of change of r with respect to z when z = 3 is 6.

options.label: \( k'(3) = 6 \), so the rate of change of z with respect to r when z = 3 is 6.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable

options.label: \( k'(3) = 6 \), so the rate of change of r with respect to z when z = 3 is 6.
\( \frac{k(3)}{3} = 6 \), so r divided by z when z = 3 is 6.
options.derivation: the Leibniz fraction read as the quotient of the two quantities at the point

options.label: \( k'(z) = 6 \), so the rate of change of r with respect to z, the same at every z, is 6.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the derivative function
